properties.decision:
RECORDED AS BRAINSTORMING, NOT AS A PROPOSAL. Raised 2026-09-22 when Anthony stopped development to get testing under control.

THE TWO THINGS NOBODY HAS MEASURED, and they are different questions with different instruments.

**REACH.** 2,442 test functions exist against 88,815 lines in 134 source files, and NOTHING has ever measured which lines they touch. `cargo-llvm-cov` is not installed and no CI step produces a coverage number. So "heavily tested" is a claim about VOLUME and cannot be quoted as a claim about coverage — the tests could be concentrated in a handful of modules and the number would look identical.

**POWER.** A test that has never been observed failing proves nothing, and this design already knows it: `dec:idea-a-check-records-that-it-was-once-observed-failing` counted 51 of 191 Verifications describing mutation-checking IN PROSE because there was nowhere else to put it. Several CI gates carry a comment saying their author personally watched them fail once. Nothing re-runs that.

OPTIONS, NONE CHOSEN, and the first two are cheap enough to do both.

(a) MEASURE REACH ONCE. Install cargo-llvm-cov, produce a per-module number, record it as a dated measurement. Turns "nobody knows" into a fact and says WHERE the 2,442 tests actually point. ⭐ Cheapest thing on this list and the only one that tells you whether the rest of the plan is aimed correctly. ⚠️ Counter: a coverage percentage is famously gameable and invites chasing the number; recording it as a measurement rather than a target is the mitigation.

(b) COVERAGE AS A RATCHET, NOT A THRESHOLD. No minimum percentage — instead, coverage of a file may not FALL. Answers the gaming objection directly and matches the grandfathering this repo already uses twice. ⚠️ Counter: needs the baseline from (a) and a stored artifact per commit.

(c) PROVE THE GATES CAN GO RED — already open as `dec:idea-does-the-build-prove-each-gate-can-go-red`, raised 2026-09-21, with its own cheap form (every gate must exit non-zero on empty or nonsense input) and expensive form (a seeded mutation per gate). ⚠️ Counter recorded there: a gate on gates is exactly the over-engineering shape to be wary of; the cheap form is one harness for a whole class.

(d) MUTATION TESTING ON THE CORE CRATE. `cargo-mutants` against reflow2-core would say what fraction of seeded faults the 2,442 tests actually catch — the strongest possible answer to "do these tests do anything". ⚠️ Counter: slow (hours), noisy, and it would produce a long list nobody has time to triage. Worth it once as a measurement; probably never as a gate.

⭐ WHY THIS MATTERS MORE THAN THE COUNT. The outside critique was that this reads as an AI coding project. The sharpest version of that criticism is not "too few tests" — it is tests that assert what the code already does and were never seen to fail. (a) and (c) are the two cheapest instruments that could refute it with evidence rather than with volume.
properties.name: OPEN — how do we know the 2,442 tests CATCH anything? Nothing measures which lines they reach, and nothing re-proves a test can still go red
properties.rationale: Recorded because the other three questions are about the RECORD of testing and this one is about the testing itself — and if the tests turn out to be concentrated or unable to fail, fixing the record would produce a well-documented false picture rather than a fixed one. Option (a) is listed first deliberately: it is an hour's work and it decides whether the rest of this plan is aimed at a real gap or an imagined one.
